step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an IoT cellular network backend. Devices connect through Mobile Network Operators (MNO). Control plane traffic (GTP CreateSession) routes through an AWS NLB into an ECS cluster, which queries Amazon Aurora for SIM configuration and coordinates session parameters with an EC2 User Plane cluster. User plane data traffic flows from MNO via an IPX network through AWS Direct Connect to the EC2 User Plane instances, which forward the user data to the Customer Backend. An Admin and the Customer Backend manage SIM configurations via Amazon API Gateway, which updates Amazon Aurora.

edges.notes: MNO sends roaming IP traffic into IPX
IPX forwards IP traffic to Direct Connect
Direct Connect delivers IP packet traffic to EC2 User Plane
MNO sends GTP CreateSession request to UDP NLB
NLB responds back to MNO with session assignment parameters
NLB forwards CreateSession GTP request to ECS Control Plane
ECS Control Plane queries Amazon Aurora for SIM configuration
Aurora returns configuration settings to ECS Control Plane
ECS Control Plane pushes session configuration down to EC2 User Plane
EC2 User Plane forwards packet payload to Customer Backend
Admin updates configurations via API Gateway
Customer Backend manages SIM configuration via API Gateway
API Gateway updates device policy and SIM configuration in Aurora
